That money should come out of the congressman's personal pocket, not the taxpayer, and plus the fact that that congressman person needs to be investigated. explicit_propositions.text: It is outrageous that a congressperson has engaged in sexual misconduct toward a staff member.
Money paid in settlements should come from a congressman's personal pocket, not taxpayer funds.
Congresspeople have used taxpayer funds to settle allegations of sexual misconduct.
A congressman who pays a settlement should be presumed guilty.
My legislation requires that congressional misconduct settlements be funded by the individual’s personal funds.
The public should be informed when a congressman faces misconduct allegations.
My legislation makes settlement payouts retroactive and mandates publication of the congressman’s name.
If a complaint reaches the ethics committee and evidence of misconduct exists, the congressman should be expelled from Congress.
Confidentiality agreements in misconduct cases primarily protect the congressman rather than the victim.
There is a second bill allowing victims to sue even after signing confidentiality agreements.

assumptions.text: Public disclosure of misconduct strengthens accountability and deters future abuse.
Taxpayer-funded settlements undermine democratic integrity and represent misuse of public resources.
Presumption of guilt based on settlement payments reflects a reasonable inference due to lack of transparency.
Victims deserve legal recourse independent of confidentiality clauses imposed during settlements.
Naming individuals involved in misconduct serves a public interest in transparency and justice.
Ethics committees possess legitimate authority and capacity to investigate and expel members.
Personal financial liability increases moral responsibility among elected officials.
Confidentiality agreements in harassment cases inherently favor institutional protection over survivor safety.
Legislators are expected to uphold high ethical standards beyond mere legal compliance.
Public outrage over misconduct indicates shared societal norms against workplace sexual misconduct.
